description: Call quality diagnostic view: per-observer A, V and Q and per-participant S for one meeting over a hold window, using the scorer's definitions and red bands. Not the verdict.

options.content:
**Diagnostic view, not the verdict.** Validity gates, observer/talker roles and cells (U×U, U×S) come from the run manifest. Run the scorer (`scripts/quality/call_quality_score.py`) for PASS/FAIL/INVALID.

- **Time range = the hold.** Set the time range to the hold: `from=<hold_start ms>&to=<hold_end ms>`. Hold values are evaluated at the end of the range over the whole range.
- **observers (regex)**: receiver user ids for A, V and Q. **talkers (regex)**: publisher user ids for A; set it to the declared continuous talkers, because a participant who is not talking counts as concealed audio here. **S participants (regex)**: whose S is shown; the scorer's G-Q9 uses every unshaped participant.
- Values follow the scorer's definitions and red bands but are not exact: for A and V, PromQL drops missing samples and pairs that the scorer counts as loss, and the 15 s grid of A and Q is aligned to the epoch, not to the hold.
- **Reconnects.** For A, V and Q, only each observer's most recently started session that is still reporting counts, as in the scorer, except when: two sessions of one observer are first seen in the same scrape (one is kept here; the scorer drops the samples where they disagree and fails G-Q8); a publisher reconnects (both of its sessions count here; the scorer fails G-Q8); an observer session has no `videocall_client_packets_sent_per_sec` (its pairs are missing here; the scorer still scores them); or a newer session reports `videocall_client_packets_sent_per_sec` before, or without, its per-pair series (the old session's values are dropped here from the newer session's first report, so the observer has no A, V or Q samples until the newer pairs appear, or for the rest of the hold if they never do; the scorer keeps the old session's values and fails G-Q8 when the newer pairs never appear).
- Server health: see the Meeting Investigation dashboard (link above).

panels.title: Audio (A): concealed share of talker audio
A per observer over time
panels.description:
Per observer, the share of talker audio that was concealed or not delivered. Per pair and 15 s sample: max(min(expand_ops / 100, 1), max(0, 1 - videocall_neteq_packets_per_sec / 50)), or 1 when videocall_peer_can_listen is not 1. Only publishers matching talkers count, and a silent gap of a declared talker counts as loss. videocall_audio_concealment_pct is deliberately not used (it overstates about 2x and its denominator moves). panels.title: Worst decoded tile staleness per observer (diagnostic)
panels.description: Max videocall_video_content_staleness_ms over an observer's tiles, only while the tile decodes (decoded video fps > 0).

targets.expr: max by (from_peer) (videocall_video_content_staleness_ms{meeting_id="$meeting",from_peer=~"$obs"} and on (session_id, from_peer, to_peer) (videocall_video_fps{meeting_id="$meeting",from_peer=~"$obs"} > 0))

panels.title: Client to relay RTT (diagnostic)
panels.description: videocall_client_active_server_rtt_ms per observer and transport.

targets.expr: max by (peer_id, server_type) (videocall_client_active_server_rtt_ms{meeting_id="$meeting",peer_id=~"$obs"})

panels.title: Participants, worst A first
panels.description:
One row per participant: A, V and Q for observers, S for S participants, over the hold. A missing pair shows as no data, never as 0, where the scorer counts it as loss. Set the time range to the hold: `from=<hold_start ms>&to=<hold_end ms>`. Hold values are evaluated at the end of the range over the whole range.
